html:
The Qin dynasty was the first imperial dynasty of China. It unified the country in 221 BCE and collapsed in 206 BCE, after only fifteen years and two emperors, but it set the template for Chinese government for the next two millennia.

Before it was an empire, Qin was a state on the western edge of the Zhou world, in the Wei River valley. It is shown on the map in 323 and 300 BCE as one of the warring states. For centuries it was a minor power. In the 4th century BCE the reforms of Shang Yang remade it: land to farmers, ranks earned through service in war, harsh collective punishments, and a state run by appointed officials. Qin became the strongest military power in China.

From 230 BCE King Ying Zheng conquered the six other states. In 221 BCE he declared himself the First Emperor, Qin Shi Huang. With Li Si he applied Qin methods to all of China:

  • commanderies under appointed governors instead of hereditary lords
  • one script, one currency, one system of weights and measures
  • roads, canals and walls, including an early Great Wall

The cost fell on the people, in taxes and forced labour. When the First Emperor died in 210 BCE, a palace plot put a weak son on the throne. In 209 BCE the uprising of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang broke out, and revolts spread everywhere. In 206 BCE the last Qin ruler surrendered.

The Han dynasty that followed condemned Qin harshness but kept most of its system. Even the name China probably comes from Qin.
sum: The Qin dynasty was the first imperial dynasty of China. It unified the country in 221 BCE and collapsed in 206 BCE, after only fifteen years and two emperors, but it set the template for Chinese government for the next two millennia.
